logo_type.rationale: The Thoughtseed horizontal wordmark carries primary brand identity. The tree mark (circular canopy with structured trunk and root system) is the icon variant. The wordmark reads first; the tree mark carries the brand at small sizes and in monochromatic contexts. Both are codified from the original logo references and never regenerated. Generated logo-object imagery (dark metal emblem, metallic 3D, glass, wax seal, concrete-botanical installation) are art-direction references and material expressions of the canonical mark, never replacement logos.

visual_concepts: The tree mark as a living organism — disciplined form filled with organic growth (concrete-botanical installation)
The tree mark as a precision artifact — machined dark metal, polished chrome, embossed glass
The tree mark as a heritage object — wax seal impression for editorial contexts
The tree mark as a collectible — holo-vinyl sticker for social media and merch
symbol_ideas: Concrete-botanical installation: weathered architectural concrete with the tree canopy filled by living moss + ferns, trunk and roots as concrete negative space
Dark metal emblem: Deep Quantum Blue-tinted polished chrome with cinematic bloom on edges
Metallic 3D object: teal chrome with mirror finish on Mindful Gray background
Glass logo: embossed glass bezel on Deep Quantum Blue surface
Wax seal: Energetic Orange wax with raised tree mark relief
Holo-vinyl sticker: prismatic sticker with peeled corner on white background

style_direction.complexity: simple — the canonical mark is minimal and structural; generated logo objects add material complexity as art direction
style_direction.weight: medium — the tree mark carries visible weight without becoming heavy
style_direction.shape: geometric-organic — circular canopy (geometric) with structured trunk and root system (organic-mechanical)

references.what_works: Horizontal layout reads cleanly; serif character carries editorial weight
references.gap_opportunity: Material expressions (concrete-botanical, metallic 3D) extend the mark into premium surfaces without replacing it

references.what_works: Circular canopy + trunk + roots reads as both architecture and growth
references.gap_opportunity: Logo-object workflows translate this geometry across premium materials while preserving proportions

concept_directions.name: Concrete-Botanical Installation
concept_directions.concept: Architectural concrete wall with the tree canopy as living moss + ferns and trunk/roots as concrete negative space
concept_directions.style_notes: Museum-grade, brutalist or gallery-clean, moss in vivid Growth Light
concept_directions.generation_prompt: Photorealistic architectural visualization with the Thoughtseed tree mark deeply recessed into weathered architectural concrete. The canopy is filled with dense living moss in #B8E986 and small ferns. The trunk and roots are formed by the negative space of the concrete. Museum-grade, premium editorial. Material variable: [BRAND_NAME=Thoughtseed], [MATERIAL_COLOR=vivid Growth Light #B8E986].

concept_directions.style_notes: Deep Quantum Blue-tinted chrome, white void background, film grain overlay

Transparent prismatic finish with cyan, turquoise, magenta, violet, emerald, amber, gold, and pearlescent white reflections. Cleanly peeled upper corner. White background.

usage_specs.minimum_size: Wordmark: 80px wide. Tree mark: 24px height. Logo objects: 320px minimum for material detail to read.
usage_specs.clear_space: Minimum clear space = 1× the height of the tree mark, on all sides. For wordmark: 1× the cap-height of the wordmark.
dont_do: Do not regenerate the canonical wordmark or tree mark. They are codified.
Do not use logo objects as replacements for the canonical mark in formal contexts (decks, contracts, press kits).
Do not stretch, skew, or recolor the canonical mark outside the approved palette.
Do not apply the mark at low contrast (<4.5:1) on backgrounds.
Do not place logo objects inside purple SaaS gradients.
Do not bake text into logo object renders — the canonical typography is always rendered separately.
